mr:0104-emmanuel-gonzalez-garcia.note: Numbered 12* in the Latin editio altera 2004 print, 11* in the Italian (CEI) edition. Manuel González García, blessed in the 2004 editions, was canonized in 2016.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin 'In monasterio Lutrensi, in Burgundia' is Lure, in Burgundy, not Brittany.

mr:0122-ladislaus-batthyany-strattmann.note: Asterisked entry (15*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin Brixia is Brescia, not Brixen.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_2004_en_unofficial: Renders the cognomen as "the Youth" (Latin cognoménto Iúvenis, Italian (CEI) detto il Giovane); "the Younger" is the conventional English epithet, which the English subject follows.
Translation error: "under Emperor Leo III the Isaurian", where the Latin print has Leónis imperatóris Sexti and the Italian (CEI) Leone VI: the emperor is Leo VI the Wise.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin is Antoninus, not Antonius (Anthony).

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1749: This edition prints the eulogy of Alexius Falconieri alone, one of the seven founders; the 2004 edition commemorates the seven founders together.

mr:0323-rebecca-de-himlaya.note: Plain entry (11., no asterisk) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition marks the entry with an asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_2004_en_unofficial: Translation error: "Saint Peter the Younger" for the subject; the Latin print has sancti Bedæ iunióris and the Italian (CEI) san Beda il Giovane. The English subject follows the Latin.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin has 'Episcopi et Confessoris', not a martyr.

mr:0502-boleslaus-strzelecki.note: Asterisked entry (12*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0512-imelda-lambertini.note: Asterisked entry (10*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0524-servulus.note: Asterisked entry (4*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin has 'Maximini' (Maximinus of Trier), but the English says 'Maximus'.

mr:0610-marcus-antonius-durando.note: Entry 9* at June 10 in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition prints the same eulogy at December 10, entry 9* (mr:1210-marcus-antonius-durando).

mr:0611-bardo.note: Asterisked entry (4*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0624-gohardus.note: Asterisked entry (7*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin 'Apud Rhegium' (Reggio) is rendered 'Riez'.
editions.martyrologium_romanum_1749: This eulogy conflates Prosper of Reggio with Prosper of Aquitaine, the anti-Pelagian writer.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin 'Ortonam, apud Frentanos' is Ortona, not Tortona.
Translation error: the Latin 'Eugenii Papae Tertii' is Eugenius III.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_2004_it_IT: Absent from the Latin editio altera 2004 print, whose July 9 ends at entry 10*. Bl. Marija Petković was beatified on 6 June 2003.

mr:0711-leontius.note: Asterisked entry (5*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_2004_it_IT: Absent from the Latin editio altera 2004 print, whose July 12 numbering begins at 2 with the gap left unrenumbered.

mr:0718-tarsicia-mackiv.note: Asterisked entry (13*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Misprint: 'Marcina' for Macrina.

mr:0730-godeleva.note: Asterisked entry (6*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0802-betharius.note: Asterisked entry (8*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0807-donatus-vesontione.note: Asterisked entry (7*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0812-iacobus-do-mai-nam-et-socii.note: Plain entry (11., no asterisk) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition marks the entry with an asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1749: This text joins the opening of Privatus's eulogy to the body of the eulogy of Paternus of Fondi (mr:0821-paternus): a line has evidently dropped. The 1914 English prints both eulogies.

mr:0821-iosephus-dang-dinh-vien.note: Plain entry (11., no asterisk) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition marks the entry with an asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: 'Domitian' where the Latin has 'persecutione Diocletiani' (Diocletian).

editions.martyrologium_romanum_2004_it_IT: Absent from the Latin editio altera 2004 print, where the day's numbered entries begin at 3 (Genesius) after the two unnumbered memorias.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin 'Constantiae, in Germania' is Konstanz, not Coutances.
Translation error: the Latin 'Apud Sirmium' is Sirmium, not Smyrna.

mr:0909-franciscus-garate-aranguren.note: Asterisked entry (10*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:1003-candida.note: The 1749 and 1914 editions commemorate a male martyr, Candidus; the 2004 edition has Candida, a woman, in the cemetery of Pontianus. It is probably the 2004 correction of the same commemoration.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin (and the 2004 entry) name Florentius, not Florentinus.

mr:1021-wendelinus.note: Asterisked entry (8*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:1026-eata.note: Asterisked entry (7*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin 'Poetovione, in Pannonia' is Pettau (Ptuj), not Poitiers.

mr:1103-libertinus.note: Asterisked entry (3*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:1103-odrada.note: Asterisked entry (10*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:1105-theotimus-et-socii.note: In the 1749 and 1914 editions this eulogy opens with Domninus, whom the 2004 edition commemorates separately (mr:1105-domninus); the rest of the group is Theotimus and companions.

mr:1118-theofredus.note: Asterisked entry (6*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:1119-eudo.note: Asterisked entry (6*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:1203-lucius.note: Plain entry (5., no asterisk) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition marks the entry with an asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_2004_it_IT: The Latin print and the English edition give this eulogy at 10 June (mr:0610-marcus-antonius-durando).

mr:1212-simon-phan-dac-hoa.note: Plain entry (11., no asterisk) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition marks the entry with an asterisk.

mr:1215-marinus.note: Asterisked entry (3*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Misprints: 'Gratian' for Gatianus and 'Fabrian' for Fabianus.

mr:1230-egwinus.note: Asterisked entry (7*) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print; the Italian (CEI) edition carries no asterisk.

mr:0103-cyrinus-et-socii.note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to the sole Theogenes

mr:0114-triginta-octo-monachi-montis-sin.note: The 2004 edition joins the monks of Sinai (38) and of Raithu (43) in one eulogy (mr:0114-monachi-raithi); the historical editions print them as two eulogies.

mr:0114-euphrasius-africae.note: The historical editions commemorate a bishop Euphrasius in Africa on this day; in the same eulogy the 2004 edition commemorates Euphrasius, bishop of Clermont (mr:0114-euphrasius).

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: "Whose birthday is the 7th of this month" seems to be an error, as this would point to Canute Lavard (mr:0107-canutus-lavard), who was not a king.

mr:0123-agathangelus.note: The 2004 eulogy mr:0123-clemens-et-agathangelus joins Clement and Agathangelus; the historical editions give Agathangelus a eulogy of his own.

mr:0205-genuinus-et-albuinus.note: The 1914 English fuses the eulogies of Ingenuinus and Albuinus of Brixen, which the 1749 edition and the 2004 edition print separately (mr:0205-ingenuinus, mr:0205-albuinus).

mr:0214-valentinus-interamnae.note: The 2004 edition has a single Valentine (on the via Flaminia), generally identified with the bishop of Terni; the 1749 and 1914 editions print both eulogies on this day.

mr:0220-eleutherius-et-socii.note: The 1749 edition names Eleutherius, bishop, and 128 others in Persia on February 20; probably the eulogy of Sadoth, bishop, and 128 companions (mr:0218-sadoth-et-socii): same place, king (Sapor), number and refusal to adore the sun.

mr:0504-triginta-novem-martyres-phaenoni.note: The 1749 and 1914 editions print the thirty-nine martyrs of the mines of Phaeno as a eulogy of their own, after that of Silvanus of Gaza; the 2004 edition commemorates them together with him in mr:0504-silvanus-et-socii.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: 'Lucius' where the Latin has 'Mucii'.

mr:0813-hippolytus.note: The Hippolytus buried in the Ager Veranus is traditionally the Hippolytus of the 2004 eulogy mr:0813-pontianus-et-hippolytus, which leads with Pontian and tells a rewritten narrative.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: This text is the rewritten eulogy of the Twelve Brothers of Benevento and does not name Donatus or Felix; it succeeds the 1749 eulogy, which mentions the twelve brothers' feast and Benevento, but its subject differs.

mr:0905-quinctius-et-socii.note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to Quintus alone (mr:0905-quintus).

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: This text joins the Octave and the Seven Sorrows in one sentence, with no clean point to split it; the Seven Sorrows half corresponds to mr:0915-maria-perdolens.
Translation error: the 1749 Latin calls him 'Episcopi Abrincensis et Confessoris', not a martyr.

mr:0928-marcus-et-socii.note: The 2004 edition drops Mark and leads with the three brothers.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin is a translation of relics (Translatio), not a birthday.

mr:1030-maximus-apameae.note: The historical editions place Maximus at Apamea; the 2004 edition places him at Cumae (mr:1030-maximus).
